correctness.rationale: The Paley autocorrelation count is (q-3)/4 on each nonzero difference, by cancellation of the two linear character sums and the squarefree quadratic sum -1. Additive orthogonality gives q k^{-4} times the autocorrelation energy under the stated target counting and source 1/k normalizations. Subtracting the fiber Cauchy–Schwarz identities and the variance of |f|^2 gives the two exact nonnegative terms, with sharp constant q(q^2-2q+5)/(q-1)^3 and constant-function witness. For q=3 the support is a singleton; q=7 has singleton nonzero difference fibers, leaving all phases of flat-modulus inputs unconstrained. Otherwise equality gives flat modulus and a well-defined phase ratio c_d on each nonzero difference. A point common to D,D+a,D+a+b gives c_(a+b)=c_a c_b; inversion covers the zero cases. Hasse's squarefree cubic bound gives triple intersections at least (q-15-2 sqrt(q))/8, positive from q=27, valid over extensions as well as primes. The exact reviewer replay `python3 /workspace/review-evidence/3.py` checks all 306 and 462 distinct ordered shift pairs at q=19,23 (minimum one in each), and derives and checks the order-11 normalized torus relation determinant -11. Its index is 11; 11 distinct normalized character restrictions attain equality. Finally d↦psi(ad) exhausts the additive dual: the parameter map is injective by surjectivity of multiplication by each nonzero a and nontriviality of psi, and the dual has order q. D-D=F_q proves uniqueness up to the specified scalar. The finite replay does not verify Hasse's theorem or prove the all-order result; the analytic steps do.
